payload.friendly_name: Squad doctrine: single owner and profile-per-task rule
payload.purpose_context: Squad guidance is split across a procedure, a styleguide, a harness skill, directives, tactics and profiles, and the copies contradict each other on point-cuts, squad size and casting. This mission consolidates the playbook into the procedure, deletes the redundant styleguide with a consumer-safe migration, shrinks the skill to a pointer, and repoints every inbound reference so consumers receive one consistent rule.
payload.purpose_tldr: Make the adversarial-squad-deployment procedure the single owner of squad doctrine and state the profile-per-task rule; sizes become examples.

payload.question: What is the mission scope for #5219?

payload.final_answer: Operator steer (issue #5219 + grounding brief, 2026-09-28): full issue scope — procedure is sole owner (profile-per-task rule, single point-cut list with pre-spec before specify, sizes and point-cut->profile table as examples, model tier delegated to model-task-routing); delete styleguide adversarial-squad-cadence and repoint its 4 inbound edges; shrink skill to triggers + pointer; trim DIRECTIVE_040, both fixed-lens tactics and Debbie/Paula profiles to reference the procedure; move glossary term to built-in; DRG edge changes per issue.

payload.question: How do projects that activated adversarial-squad-cadence survive its deletion?

payload.final_answer: Upgrade migration that strips the retired styleguide id from config.yaml, charter.yaml (activation + catalog) and references.yaml, following the m_3_2_6_retire_rtk_search_tooling precedent (the charter compiler fails closed on an unknown activated id). This repository's own charter surfaces are updated in the same change.

payload.question: Downgrade DIRECTIVE_001 -> paula-patterns-architecture-scout-review from requires to suggests?

payload.final_answer: Yes — the scout tactic is recurrence-only and expensive; an always-on architectural directive should point at it, not require it. Keep only if the reachability goldens show the tactic would stop being delivered.

payload.question: Should the procedure reserve or write the #5221 disposition contract section?

payload.final_answer: Do not write it. #5221 owns the disposition contract; this mission leaves the procedure's record step intact and adds no placeholder prose to shipped doctrine.
Operator 2026-09-28: yes — one mission, one PR covering #5219, #5220, #5221 (epic #5218), #5202 and #5078.

payload.question: #5202: which guidelines.md tree is the single owner?

payload.final_answer: Operator: mission-steps/. Merge correct halves into mission-steps/, repoint the loader, delete every actions/*/guidelines.md, replace the byte-identity guard with an absence guard + loader-path test.

payload.question: #5078: is safe-commit consumer doctrine, and who opens PRs for workflow-changing WPs?

payload.final_answer: Operator: safe-commit is consumer doctrine (printed recipes become spec-kitty safe-commit <files> -m ... --to-branch <lane>, protected-main planning case spelled out); the WP agent pushes only and the orchestrator opens the draft PR and records the run ID.

Operator: also do renames/kind changes. Retire adversarial-squad-cadence, bug-fixing-checklist (into test-first-bug-fixing), locality-of-change tactic (into avoid-gold-plating), common-docs-curation (into scaffold/write/find); rename iterative-deepening-review and move it with tracker-organisation-workflow to packs/internal; change boring-code-review to a styleguide; rename behavior-driven-development tactic to bdd-scenario-formulation under tactics/testing/. All covered by one data-driven consumer migration.

payload.question: #5220 item 1: where does tidy-first sit in a bug fix?

payload.final_answer: Default: DIRECTIVE_025 owns it. Tidy-first is a separate behaviour-preserving commit on the surfaces the fix will touch, before the red repro; refactor-after-green in test-first-bug-fixing is limited to the fix's own code.

payload.question: #5220 item 3: test and fix committed together?

payload.final_answer: Default: together, unless a failing reproduction test already landed on the mainline under red-main-release-discipline; then the fix commit turns that test green.
Default: no numeric target. One band table in the mutation-testing-workflow tactic, framed as triage bands; a CI break gate is a project opt-in with break: 0 as the shipped default.

payload.question: #5221 C1: does Node LTS stay a directive pillar?

payload.final_answer: Default: no. DIRECTIVE_051 states ecosystem-neutral pillars once; Node LTS moves into a JS/TS toolguide next to the per-ecosystem steps.

payload.wp_title: Printed commit recipes use safe-commit (#5078 code)
Supply-chain doctrine owner: DIRECTIVE_051, neutral tactic, per-ecosystem toolguides (#5221 C)
Served prompts, step contracts and profiles reference the owners (#5221 C/E, #5078 prompt, #5220 profiles)
DRG wiring, activation packs and regeneration (single owner of generated surfaces)
Squad doctrine single owner (#5219 content + disposition contract)
Dogfood the migration, charter, docs and glossary
Testing, bug-fixing and BDD doctrine owners (#5220)
Change-scope reconciler, review tactics, kind change and in-house moves (#5221 B, D)
